trust_decision.summary: Which keys of a caller-supplied options object may be copied during the recursive config merge; ConfigMerge recurses into target[key] whenever both sides pass isPlainObject, and Object.prototype passes it, so a nested __proto__ key makes the merge write into Object.prototype.

landing_point.why: The advisory title names Jodit.configure(), a one-line static method that hands options to ConfigMerge.

fix_sites.entry_point: Jodit.configure(options) (src/jodit.ts:256-258); ConfigMerge is also exported publicly through the helpers barrel (src/core/helpers/utils/index.ts:18)
Jodit.make(el, options) -> initOptions -> ConfigProto (src/jodit.ts:1221-1224); also Jodit.modules.Helpers.ConfigProto and the View/Dialog/Uploader/FileBrowser/Ajax option builders
fix_sites.module_kind: per-instance prototype-chain config builder (hardening; it builds a fresh object and never writes into proto)

fix_sites.entry_point: internal helper isUnsafeProtoKey shared by both sites

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both changed functions are in src/core/helpers/utils/config-proto.ts, the file the advisory names (ConfigMerge). The ConfigProto site at src/core/helpers/utils/config-proto.ts:79-97 is the same file and only hardening.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue that ConfigProto never writes into proto: it builds newOpt and then calls Object.setPrototypeOf (src/core/helpers/utils/config-proto.ts:77-99), so they skip it. Hidden tests probably cannot tell the difference.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Partial deep updates must keep working: Jodit.configure({controls:{x:{group}}}) patches one control in place and keeps the others, and Jodit.atom values replace instead of merging. A fix that stops recursing, swaps in Object.create(null) or rejects nested objects breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: __proto__ nested under an existing plain-object option (e.g. controls) via JSON.parse own key
constructor / prototype keys at any depth (rejected defensively)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: extendLang shallow-merges a caller dictionary into the global lang table with Object.assign(lang[key], ...). A '__proto__' key resolves lang['__proto__'] to Object.prototype and assigns into it.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the same 'merge plugin-supplied dictionaries into a global' idea, written separately in another package (core/global) and used by several plugins. A maintainer patching config-proto would not look here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The public Helpers.set(path, value, obj) walks a dot path; isPlainObject(Object.prototype) is true, so a '__proto__.x' path writes into Object.prototype.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is a how-type parser differential on the key's identity (the dot split happens before any key check). It is exposed as Jodit.modules.Helpers.set (src/core/helpers/utils/index.ts:35) and is a classic shape for a deep-set helper.

O9_family: CWE-1321 prototype pollution via recursive config merge

O10_build.toolchain: Node + npm, make, esbuild, karma + mocha in Chrome headless (package.json:13-14, package.json:94-99)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Strip '__proto__' only from the top-level keys inside Jodit.configure(), which misses the nested controls.__proto__ shape that ConfigMerge recurses into.

out_of_scope_notes: Helpers.set (src/core/helpers/utils/set.ts:40-51) appears to allow a '__proto__.x' path write into Object.prototype. It is a separate helper that configure/ConfigMerge never reaches, so it is not pursued.
extendLang (src/core/global.ts:61-69) does Object.assign into lang[key] with no key filter. Its inputs are plugin-bundled language packs, not user config, so it is not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell use); tiny_repo/giant_repo not assessed.

needs_gpu_kernel_gui: the project tests run in karma Chrome headless (package.json:14). ConfigMerge itself is pure JS but imports jodit/config, which pulls in DOM-dependent modules; a headless browser or jsdom harness is probably needed. Flagged conservatively.
offline_after_build: likely true (no network in the merge path), but karma/browser setup was not checked.
ConfigProto site judged non-exploitable by reading only (newOpt is fresh and gets setPrototypeOf; there is no write into proto). Not executed.
single_site not flagged: the fix touches two functions in one file, but only ConfigMerge is a demonstrable sink, so in practice it behaves like a single-site fix.
present_in_latest not applicable: latest release is 'none'.
